technical_and_design_decisions: Adopt Spring XD 1.3.x as the runtime platform for module deployment and stream processing, aligned with user story references to Spring XD clusters and singlenode containers.
Implement all custom modules (Kafka source/sink, generator source, perf-meter sink, mass ingestion sink) as standard Spring XD modules following the framework's module development patterns.
Use Spring for Apache Kafka (spring-kafka) library for Kafka source implementation to access low-level consumer API capabilities for deterministic offset and partition management as required by U2.
Package all custom modules as executable uber-jars using Spring Boot, ensuring all dependencies are bundled for seamless cluster deployment as required by U3.
Extend the existing Spring XD admin server REST API to support custom module upload and installation, reusing existing module repository and deployment logic to minimize custom code.
Use JUnit and Spring XD's built-in module test harness for automated testing of module functionality, with tests integrated into the CI pipeline as required by U8.
Use Maven as the build tool for all modules and sample applications, consistent with Spring ecosystem standards and existing project conventions.
Implement the mass data ingestion sink (U1) using reusable Spring Integration connectors for HDFS, HAWQ, and GPDB to avoid custom data store integration code.
assumptions: The target Spring XD version is compatible with Java 17+ as mandated by Spring Framework 6.0 requirements mentioned in the specification.
Pre-existing Kafka, HDFS, HAWQ, and GPDB clusters are provisioned and accessible for development and testing, so no infrastructure setup effort is included in estimates.
The Spring XD admin server's existing module repository can be extended to support custom module uploads, eliminating the need to build a separate module storage system.
The sample GitHub project for Spring XD + Kafka provisioning (U4) will use Docker Compose for local cluster deployment to simplify setup for end users.
All user stories are part of a single software increment with no dependencies on external teams or third-party deliverables.
The performance test stream (U7) will be executed on a local singlenode Spring XD container, with no requirement for distributed cluster performance testing in this increment.
